To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
profile completeness is a strong indicator of the likelihood of a friendship link between two Facebook users.

profile elements that signal a user's social capital, such as number of friends and number of mutual friends, and profile elements that signal common ground, such as hometown and college, are most likely to be associated with friendship articulations.

the profile fields that are most predictive of friendship links on Facebook are: (1) the “About Me” text field; (2) the “Favorite Quotations” field; (3) the “Favorite Movies” field; (4) the “Relationship Status” field; and (5) the “Political Views” field.

the role of the profile as a signal of social connectedness, and the ways in which the profile can be designed to encourage articulation of social relationships.

how profile fields are used to signal commonalities between users, and how these signals are used to encourage friendship connections.

the most important elements in the profile are those which are the most personal, and those that allow for a user to express their own unique identity.
the more profile fields a person completes, the more friends that person will have.

profile elements can serve as signals of common ground, and that profile elements that are more likely to be completed (e.g., hometown) are more predictive of friendship links than elements that are less likely to be completed.

profile fields are important signals of social capital, and that designers can use this knowledge to encourage users to complete profile fields and to encourage the articulation of friendships.
